items.title: Radial kernels, polynomial augmentation, and site geometry

references.title: Narcowich, Ward, and Wendland, Sobolev bounds on functions with scattered zeros, Math. Comp. 74 (2005), §§1 and 3.1
Rasmussen and Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 4

items.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$. An admitted domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ is a nonempty bounded Lipschitz domain (its boundary is locally the graph of a Lipschitz function, with $\Omega$ on one side) with fixed $r_0>0$ and $0<\theta<\pi/2$ such that for every $x\in\overline\Omega$ there is an orthogonal map $Q_x$ for which
$$x+Q_x\{z\in\mathbb R^d:0<|z|<r_0,\ z_1>|z|\cos\theta\}\subset\Omega.$$
An orthogonal map is a real linear map with $Q_x^{\mathsf T}Q_x=I$, equivalently one preserving the Euclidean inner product. The map $Q_x$ may depend on $x$; no simultaneous selection of the maps is part of this definition.

A real radial kernel on $\mathbb R^d$ has the form $K(x,y)=\phi(|x-y|)$ for a function $\phi:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$. For a finite ordered list of distinct sites $X=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)$, its Gram matrix is $K_X=(K(x_i,x_j))_{i,j=1}^N$. The kernel is **strictly positive definite** if $c^{\mathsf T}K_Xc>0$ for every such $X$ and every nonzero $c\in\mathbb R^N$; the nonstrict positive-semidefinite condition replaces $>$ by $\ge$. Only strict positivity is used for the ordinary interpolation solve below.

For an integer $m\ge1$, let $\Pi_{m-1}(\mathbb R^d)$ be the real polynomials of total degree at most $m-1$, with an ordered basis $p_1,\ldots,p_J$, where $J=\dim\Pi_{m-1}(\mathbb R^d)$. The evaluation matrix on $X$ is $P_X=(p_j(x_i))_{i,j}$. The sites are **$m$-unisolvent** for this polynomial space when $P_X$ has linearly independent columns. A kernel is **strictly conditionally positive definite of order $m$** when, for every finite distinct $X$ and this evaluation matrix, $c^{\mathsf T}K_Xc>0$ for every nonzero $c\in\mathbb R^N$ satisfying $P_X^{\mathsf T}c=0$. Thus strict conditional positivity is a strict inequality on the moment-null subspace; it is stronger than the corresponding nonstrict inequality.

For data $y\in\mathbb R^N$, the strictly positive definite interpolation system is $K_Xa=y$. For an order-$m$ strictly conditionally positive definite kernel and $m$-unisolvent sites, the polynomially augmented interpolation system is
$$\begin{bmatrix}K_X&P_X\\P_X^{\mathsf T}&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}a\\b\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}y\\0\end{bmatrix}.$$
Whenever the relevant system has a unique solution, its kernel-plus-polynomial function $x\mapsto\sum_i a_iK(x,x_i)+\sum_j b_jp_j(x)$ is called the interpolant. Invertibility for the stated strict hypotheses is supplied by [[lem-rbf-augmented-system-is-invertible]].

For a finite nonempty site set $X\subset\Omega$, the **fill distance** is $h_X=\sup_{x\in\Omega}\min_{x_i\in X}|x-x_i|$. If $N\ge2$, the **separation radius** and **mesh ratio** are $q_X=\tfrac12\min_{i\ne j}|x_i-x_j|$ and $\rho_X=h_X/q_X$, respectively. These are exact geometric quantities, independent of any floating-point solver.

items.title: Strict positive and conditionally positive augmented interpolation systems are invertible

references.title: Narcowich, Ward, and Wendland, Sobolev bounds on functions with scattered zeros, Math. Comp. 74 (2005), §3.1
Gregory E. Fasshauer, MATH 590: Meshfree Methods, Chapter 13, pp. 18–25

items.statement: Let $X=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)$ be a finite ordered list of distinct sites in $\mathbb R^d$. If $K$ is strictly positive definite, then $K_X$ is invertible and $K_Xa=y$ has a unique solution for every $y\in\mathbb R^N$. If $K$ is strictly conditionally positive definite of order $m$ and $X$ is $m$-unisolvent for $\Pi_{m-1}(\mathbb R^d)$, then the augmented matrix in [[def-rbf-kernels-sites-and-augmented-interpolation]] is invertible and its system has a unique solution for every right-hand side.

items.title: The normalized Matérn kernel in the 2π Fourier convention

references.title: Rasmussen and Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 4, equations (4.14)–(4.15)
Gregory E. Fasshauer, MATH 590: Meshfree Methods, Chapter 13, pp. 34–36

items.statement:

u>0$, and an inverse length $a>0$. Assume Countable Choice for the Lebesgue-integration suppliers used to justify this formula; this definition does not assume full Choice. Put $s=

With the negative-sign Fourier transform convention $\widehat U(\xi)=\int U(x)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\,dx$, define the normalized stationary kernel by
$$k(z)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}w(\xi)e^{2\pi i z\cdot\xi}\,d\xi,\qquad K(x,y)=k(x-y).$$
The corresponding length parameter in the usual Matérn notation is $\ell=\sqrt{2
u}/a$. For $b>0$, define the modified Bessel function in its integral normalization by
$$K_
u(b)= rac12\left( rac b2ight)^
u\int_0^\infty u^{-
u-1}e^{-u-b^2/(4u)}\,du.$$
The classical Bessel expression for $k(z)$ when $z
e0$, its value $k(0)=1$, absolute convergence, continuity, and radial symmetry are established by [[lem-matern-spectral-integral-and-normalization]]. This definition makes no finite-precision stability claim.

items.title: Fourier Bessel-potential and restriction-quotient Sobolev spaces

references.title: Gregory E. Fasshauer, MATH 590: Meshfree Methods, Chapter 13, pp. 23–36
Rasmussen and Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 4, equations (4.5)–(4.6)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice when using the well-definedness results below; it is inherited conservatively from the published $L^2$ completeness supplier. Let $d\ge1$ and $s>d/2$. Write $L^2_s(\mathbb R^d)$ for the equivalence classes modulo Lebesgue-almost-everywhere equality of measurable complex functions $g$ satisfying
$$\|g\|_{L^2_s}^2=\int_{\mathbb R^d}(1+|\xi|^2)^s|g(\xi)|^2\,d\xi<\infty.$$
For such $g$, the **inverse Fourier representative** is the function
$$U_g(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}g(\xi)e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\,d\xi.$$
The whole-space Bessel-potential space $H^s(\mathbb R^d)$ consists of these representatives, with norm $\|U_g\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^d)}=\|g\|_{L^2_s}$. For the admitted domain $\Omega$ of [[def-rbf-kernels-sites-and-augmented-interpolation]], define $H^s(\Omega)$ to be the restrictions $U|_\Omega$ of whole-space members, with the quotient norm
$$\|u\|_{H^s(\Omega)}=\inf\{\|U\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^d)}:U|_\Omega=u\}.$$
The whole-space inner product is $\langle U_g,U_h\rangle_{H^s}=\int (1+|\xi|^2)^s g(\xi)\overline{h(\xi)}\,d\xi$, linear in the first variable as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]].
The inverse Fourier map is injective, whole-space representatives are continuous, the whole-space model is Hilbert, and Schwartz functions are dense in that norm; these facts are supplied by [[lem-matern-weighted-fourier-space-is-hilbert-and-injective]] and [[lem-schwartz-dense-in-fourier-bessel-potential-space]]. The restriction quotient is a norm by bounded point evaluation; its Hilbert realization as the restricted native space is proved in [[lem-restricted-matern-native-space-is-sobolev]]. No extension operator or identification with an intrinsic fractional Sobolev norm on $\Omega$ is part of this definition.

items.title: Uniform cone domains admit stable polynomial norming stencils

references.title: Narcowich, Ward, and Wendland, Sobolev bounds on functions with scattered zeros, Math. Comp. 74 (2005), §§2.1–2.2

items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be an admitted domain of [[def-rbf-kernels-sites-and-augmented-interpolation]], let $X\subset\Omega$ be finite and nonempty, and put $h=h_X$. Fix an integer $m\ge1$ and let $J=\dim\Pi_{m-1}(\mathbb R^d)$. There are constants $R,B,h_0>0$, depending only on $d,m,r_0,\theta$, such that if $0<h\le h_0$, then for every $x\in\overline\Omega$ there are distinct nodes $y_1,\ldots,y_J\in X$ and real weights $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_J$ with
$$|y_j-x|\le Rh,\qquad \sum_{j=1}^J|\lambda_j|\le B,\qquad p(x)=\sum_{j=1}^J\lambda_jp(y_j)\quad(p\in\Pi_{m-1}(\mathbb R^d)).$$
No lower bound on site separation is assumed.

items.title: The Matérn spectral integral, normalization, and radial formula

references.title: Rasmussen and Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 4, equations (4.5)–(4.15)
Gregory E. Fasshauer, MATH 590: Meshfree Methods, Chapter 13, pp. 24–36

$$\int_{\mathbb R^d}w(\xi)\,d\xi=1.$$
The integral defining $k(z)$ is absolutely convergent for every $z$; $k$ is real, even, radial, and continuous, and $k(0)=1$. For every $z\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$k(z)= rac{a^{2
u}}{\Gamma(
u)}\int_0^\infty t^{
u-1}\exp\!\left(-a^2t- rac{|z|^2}{4t}ight)dt.$$
For $z
e0$ this is equivalently
$$k(z)= rac{2^{1-
u}}{\Gamma(
u)}(a|z|)^
u K_
u(a|z|),$$
where $K_
u$ has the integral normalization in [[def-normalized-matern-spectral-kernel]]. Under the stated Fourier convention, the $d$-dimensional Gaussian identity is, for $t>0$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{-4\pi^2t|\xi|^2}e^{2\pi i z\cdot\xi}\,d\xi=(4\pi t)^{-d/2}e^{-|z|^2/(4t)}.$$

items.title: Exact augmented RBF-FD weights for a local differential functional

references.title: Accelerated Training of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) using Meshless Discretizations
Narcowich, Ward, and Wendland, Sobolev bounds on functions with scattered zeros, Math. Comp. 74 (2005), §3.1

items.statement:
The **exact augmented RBF finite-difference weight procedure** has the following inputs: a dimension $d\ge1$; an integer polynomial degree $r\ge0$; a finite ordered stencil $Y=(y_1,\ldots,y_N)\subset\mathbb R^d$ of distinct sites that is $(r+1)$-unisolvent for $\Pi_r(\mathbb R^d)$; a real kernel $K$ strictly conditionally positive definite of order $r+1$; an ordered basis $p_1,\ldots,p_J$ of $\Pi_r(\mathbb R^d)$; a center $x\in\mathbb R^d$; a homogeneous constant-coefficient differential functional $L=\sum_{|\alpha|=t}c_\alpha D^\alpha$ with $0\le t\le r$; and a neighborhood of $x$ on which every section $z\mapsto K(z,y_i)$ has continuous derivatives through order $t$. Here $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^d$, $|\alpha|=\sum_j\alpha_j$, and $D^\alpha$ is the corresponding partial derivative. All arithmetic in this procedure is exact real arithmetic.

If dimensions, distinctness, unisolvence, the kernel condition, or derivative availability fail, return `inadmissible-input`. Otherwise form $P_{ij}=p_j(y_i)$, $b_i=(L_zK(z,y_i))|_{z=x}$, $\ell_j=(Lp_j)(x)$, and
$$M=\begin{bmatrix}K_Y&P\\P^{\mathsf T}&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad g=\begin{bmatrix}b\\ell\end{bmatrix}.$$
Solve $Mz=g$ by exact Gaussian elimination with deterministic nonzero-pivot row selection: set $A=M$, $c=g$, and $n=N+J$. For $k=1,\ldots,n$, choose the least $i\ge k$ with $A_{ik}\ne0$; if none exists, return `singular-system`. Swap rows $i$ and $k$ in both $A$ and $c$. For each $j=k+1,\ldots,n$ in increasing order, set $\mu=A_{jk}/A_{kk}$, replace row $j$ by row $j-\mu\,\mathrm{row}_k$ in $A$ and $c$, and set $A_{jk}=0$. After all pivots, set $z_n=c_n/A_{nn}$; then, for $k=n-1,n-2,\ldots,1$ in decreasing order, set $z_k=(c_k-\sum_{j=k+1}^n A_{kj}z_j)/A_{kk}$. Return `success` with the first $N$ coordinates $w$ of $z$ and the remaining $J$ polynomial multipliers. The stated strict hypotheses imply that `singular-system` is unreachable, as proved by [[lem-rbf-augmented-system-is-invertible]].

The returned $w$ is an exact mathematical weight vector. The nonsingularity lemma [[lem-rbf-augmented-system-is-invertible]] makes `singular-system` unreachable for every input that passes the stated strict hypotheses. This definition makes no floating-point stability or solver-error claim.

items.title: The weighted Fourier model is an injective Hilbert representation

references.title: Gregory E. Fasshauer, MATH 590: Meshfree Methods, Chapter 13, pp. 19–25
Rasmussen and Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 4, equations (4.5)–(4.6)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as a conservative cover of the published $L^2$ completeness dependency, which declares it in its transitive dependencies although its statement requires only Countable Choice. For every $s>d/2$, each $g\in L^2_s(\mathbb R^d)$ lies in $L^1(\mathbb R^d)$, its inverse Fourier representative $U_g$ is bounded and continuous, the map $g\mapsto U_g$ is injective, and the whole-space Fourier Bessel-potential space of [[def-bessel-potential-space-and-restriction-quotient]] is a complex Hilbert space. In particular, for a constant $C_{d,s}<\infty$,
$$|U_g(x)|\le C_{d,s}\|g\|_{L^2_s}\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^d).$$

items.title: Separated Matérn sites have an explicit positive Gram lower bound

references.title: Narcowich, Ward, and Wendland, Sobolev bounds on functions with scattered zeros, Math. Comp. 74 (2005), §3.1
Gregory E. Fasshauer, MATH 590: Meshfree Methods, Chapter 13, pp. 34–36

items.statement:
Fix $d\ge1$, $
u>0$, $a>0$, $s=
u+d/2$, and the normalized Matérn kernel with spectral density $w(\xi)=A(a^2+4\pi^2|\xi|^2)^{-s}$ from [[def-normalized-matern-spectral-kernel]]. For a list of $N\ge2$ distinct sites $X=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\subset\mathbb R^d$, put $q=	frac12\min_{i
e j}|x_i-x_j|$. There is $c=c(d,
u,a)>0$ such that if $0<q\le1$, then
$$\lambda_{\min}(K_X)\ge c q^{2
u},\qquad \lambda_{\max}(K_X)\le N,\qquad \kappa_2(K_X)\le c^{-1}Nq^{-2
u}.$$
The eigenvalues and condition number are those of the exact real symmetric positive-definite matrix. For $N=1$, $K_X=[1]$ and $\kappa_2(K_X)=1$.

items.title: Augmented RBF-FD weights reproduce polynomials and obey a local Taylor bound

references.title: Accelerated Training of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) using Meshless Discretizations
Narcowich, Ward, and Wendland, Sobolev bounds on functions with scattered zeros, Math. Comp. 74 (2005), §3.1

items.statement:
Let $p\ge0$ be an integer, let $Y=(y_1,\ldots,y_N)$ be distinct and $(p+1)$-unisolvent for $\Pi_p(\mathbb R^d)$, and let $K$ be a real strictly conditionally positive-definite kernel of order $p+1$. Fix a center $x$, an ordered basis $p_1,\ldots,p_J$ of $\Pi_p$, and a homogeneous constant-coefficient differential functional $L$ of order $t\le p$ for which all section derivatives in [[alg-augmented-rbf-finite-difference-weights]] exist. Let $(w,v)$ be the exact output of that procedure and put $r_Y=\max_i|y_i-x|$. Then the procedure returns success, and for every $q\in\Pi_p$,
$$\sum_{i=1}^Nw_iq(y_i)=Lq(x).$$
If $f\in C^{p+1}(U)$ on an open convex set $U$ containing the compact convex hull $H=\operatorname{conv}\{x,y_1,\ldots,y_N\}$, then
$$\left|\sum_iw_if(y_i)-Lf(x)\right|\le C_{d,p}\left(\sum_i|w_i|\right)r_Y^{p+1}\max_{|\alpha|=p+1}\sup_{z\in H}|D^\alpha f(z)|.$$
Consequently, when $r_Y>0$, a separately proved bound $\sum_i|w_i|\le C_wr_Y^{-t}$ yields the order $C_{d,p}C_wr_Y^{p+1-t}$ truncation bound. Unisolvence alone is not asserted to provide this weight-norm bound.

items.title: Schwartz functions are dense in the Fourier Bessel-potential norm

references.title: Gregory E. Fasshauer, MATH 590: Meshfree Methods, Chapter 13, pp. 23–36

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the declared $L^2$ dependency. For every $s>d/2$, every Schwartz function $f$ belongs to $H^s(\mathbb R^d)$, and the inverse Fourier transforms of $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ are Schwartz functions and are dense in $H^s(\mathbb R^d)$ of [[def-bessel-potential-space-and-restriction-quotient]]. The Fourier transform uses the negative-sign $2\pi$ convention.

items.title: A Sobolev function vanishing on scattered sites has an h^ν bound

references.title: Narcowich, Ward, and Wendland, Sobolev bounds on functions with scattered zeros, Math. Comp. 74 (2005), §§2.1–2.2
Gregory E. Fasshauer, MATH 590: Meshfree Methods, Chapter 13, pp. 23–25

items.statement:
Assume full AC conservatively for the declared weighted-$L^2$ Hilbert dependency. Let $\Omega$ be an admitted domain with its uniform cone constants, fix $d\ge1$, $
u>0$, $s=
u+d/2$, and choose an integer $m>
u$. There exist $C,h_0>0$, depending only on $d,s,m$ and the cone constants, such that for every finite nonempty $X\subset\Omega$ of fill distance $h=h_X\le h_0$ and every $u\in H^s(\Omega)$ with $u|_X=0$,
$$\|u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\le C h^
u\|u\|_{H^s(\Omega)}.$$
The estimate has no separation or mesh-ratio hypothesis.

items.title: Bounded mesh ratio gives an h^{-2s} exact condition-number bound

references.title: Narcowich, Ward, and Wendland, Sobolev bounds on functions with scattered zeros, Math. Comp. 74 (2005), §3.1
Gregory E. Fasshauer, MATH 590: Meshfree Methods, Chapter 13, pp. 34–36

items.statement:
Fix Matérn parameters $d\ge1$, $
u>0$, $a>0$, $s=
u+d/2$, an admitted bounded domain $\Omega$, and a mesh-ratio bound $ho_0>0$. There is $C=C(\Omega,d,
u,a,ho_0)$ such that every finite nonempty distinct site set $X\subset\Omega$ with $N\ge2$, $0<q_X\le1$, $0<h_X\le1$, and $ho_X=h_X/q_X\leho_0$ satisfies
$$\kappa_2(K_X)\le C h_X^{-2s}.$$
The one-site case has condition number $1$. This is an exact-arithmetic condition-number estimate for the Gram matrix; it does not bound the error of a floating-point solver.

items.title: The Matérn native space has its weighted Fourier norm and strict Gram positivity

references.title: Rasmussen and Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 4, equations (4.5)–(4.8)
Gregory E. Fasshauer, MATH 590: Meshfree Methods, Chapter 13, pp. 18–25

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice conservatively for the declared $L^2$ Hilbert-space dependency. Fix $d\ge1$, $\nu>0$, $a>0$, and $s=\nu+d/2$, and let $k,w$ be the normalized Matérn kernel and positive spectral density of [[def-normalized-matern-spectral-kernel]]. Let $\mathcal H_k(\mathbb R^d)$ consist of the inverse Fourier representatives $U_g$ with $\int |g(\xi)|^2/w(\xi)\,d\xi<\infty$, with inner product
$$\langle U_g,U_h\rangle_k=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\frac{g(\xi)\overline{h(\xi)}}{w(\xi)}d\xi.$$
Then this is a Hilbert space, each kernel section $k(\cdot-y)$ reproduces evaluation at $y$, and its span is dense. There are constants $0<c\le C<\infty$, depending only on $d,\nu,a$, such that
$$c\|U\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^d)}\le\|U\|_k\le C\|U\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^d)}.$$
For every finite list of distinct sites $X=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)$, the Matérn Gram matrix $K_X=(k(x_i-x_j))$ is strictly positive definite.

items.title: The restricted Matérn native space is the Sobolev quotient space

references.title: Gregory E. Fasshauer, MATH 590: Meshfree Methods, Chapter 13, pp. 18–25 and 34–36
Narcowich, Ward, and Wendland, Sobolev bounds on functions with scattered zeros, Math. Comp. 74 (2005), §§2.1–2.2

items.statement:
Assume full AC conservatively for the declared Hilbert projection dependency. Fix the Matérn kernel of [[def-normalized-matern-spectral-kernel]] on a nonempty domain $\Omega$ of [[def-rbf-kernels-sites-and-augmented-interpolation]]. Let $\mathcal N_\Omega=\{U\in\mathcal H_k(\mathbb R^d):U|_\Omega=0\}$. The restricted native space is the quotient $\mathcal H_k(\mathbb R^d)/\mathcal N_\Omega$ with infimal extension norm, and it is the reproducing-kernel Hilbert space of $k|_{\Omega\times\Omega}$. Its norm is equivalent to the restriction-quotient norm of $H^s(\Omega)$: for constants $c,C>0$ depending only on $d,\nu,a$,
$$c\|u\|_{H^s(\Omega)}\le\|u\|_{\mathcal H_k(\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{H^s(\Omega)}.$$
No extension theorem or intrinsic fractional-domain norm is asserted.

items.title: Native Matérn interpolation is an orthogonal projection with power function

references.title: Rasmussen and Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 4, equations (4.5)–(4.8)
Gregory E. Fasshauer, MATH 590: Meshfree Methods, Chapter 13, pp. 18–25

items.statement:
Assume full AC conservatively for the declared Hilbert projection dependencies. Let $X=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\subset\Omega$ be distinct and nonempty, and let $\mathcal H_k(\Omega)$ be the restricted Matérn native RKHS. For every $f\in\mathcal H_k(\Omega)$, the unique kernel interpolant $s_Xf=\sum_jc_jk(\cdot-x_j)$ is the orthogonal projection of $f$ onto $V_X=\operatorname{span}\{k(\cdot-x_j):1\le j\le N\}$. Define
$$P_X(x)=\|(I-\Pi_X)k(\cdot-x)\|_{\mathcal H_k(\Omega)},$$
where $\Pi_X$ is that projection. Then for every $x\in\Omega$,
$$|f(x)-s_Xf(x)|\le P_X(x)\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k(\Omega)},\qquad P_X(x)^2=k(0)-k_X(x)^*K_X^{-1}k_X(x)\ge0.$$
where $K_X=(k(x_i-x_j))$ and $k_X(x)=(k(x_i-x))_{i=1}^N$.

items.title: Matérn interpolation and its power function converge at rate h^ν

references.title: Narcowich, Ward, and Wendland, Sobolev bounds on functions with scattered zeros, Math. Comp. 74 (2005), Theorem 1.1 and §§2.1–2.2
Gregory E. Fasshauer, MATH 590: Meshfree Methods, Chapter 13, pp. 34–36

items.statement:
Assume full AC conservatively for the Hilbert projection and weighted-$L^2$ suppliers. Fix arbitrary $d\ge1$, $
u>0$, $a>0$, $s=
u+d/2$, the normalized Matérn kernel $k$ of [[def-normalized-matern-spectral-kernel]], and an admitted uniform-cone domain $\Omega$. There are constants $C,h_0>0$, depending only on $d,
u,a$ and the domain's cone constants, such that for every finite nonempty distinct site set $X\subset\Omega$ with fill distance $h_X\le h_0$ and every $f\in H^s(\Omega)$,
$$\|f-s_Xf\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\le C h_X^
u\|f\|_{H^s(\Omega)},\qquad \sup_{x\in\Omega}P_X(x)\le C h_X^
u.$$
Here $s_Xf$ and $P_X$ are the native interpolant and power function of [[thm-native-interpolation-projection-and-power-function]]. The rate requires no mesh-ratio bound. The constants are uniform over site sets satisfying the fill-distance condition.

title: Radial basis and kernel interpolation — Examples

items.title: Duplicate sites make the kernel Gram matrix singular

references.title: Narcowich, Ward, and Wendland, Sobolev bounds on functions with scattered zeros, Math. Comp. 74 (2005), §1

items.statement: Let $K(x,y)=\phi(|x-y|)$ be any radial kernel, and let a site list contain $x_1=x_2$.

items.title: A small fill distance can coexist with poor separation and conditioning

references.title: Narcowich, Ward, and Wendland, Sobolev bounds on functions with scattered zeros, Math. Comp. 74 (2005), §3.1
Rasmussen and Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 4, equations (4.5)–(4.8)

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For fixed $d\ge1$, $\nu>0$, and $a>0$, let $X_m$ be the midpoint grid in $\Omega=(0,1)^d$ for each odd $m\ge3$. There are $0<\delta_m<1/(4m^2)$ such that the augmented sets $Z_m=X_m\cup\{x_0+\delta_me_1\}$, with $x_0=(1/2,\ldots,1/2)$, satisfy $h_{Z_m}\to0$, $\rho_{Z_m}\to\infty$, and $\kappa_2(K_{Z_m})\to\infty$ for the normalized Matérn kernel.

items.title: A smooth scattered surface inherits the Matérn fill-distance rate

references.title: Narcowich, Ward, and Wendland, Sobolev bounds on functions with scattered zeros, Math. Comp. 74 (2005), Theorem 1.1
Gregory E. Fasshauer, MATH 590: Meshfree Methods, Chapter 13, pp. 34–36

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as required by the Fourier-space and interpolation suppliers. Fix $d\ge1$, $\nu>0$, $a>0$, and let $\Omega=(0,1)^d$. The smooth graph $\{(x,f(x)):x\in\overline\Omega\}$ with $f(x)=e^{-\pi|x|^2}$ is interpolated from midpoint-grid samples by the normalized Matérn kernel of smoothness $\nu$.
